evidence.quote: to estimate the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA), the double-layer capacitance was determined via cyclic voltammetry at varying scan rates.

cyclic voltammograms (CVs) were recorded in the OCP region within a potential window of 0.05 V. The CV analyses were performed at scan rates ranging from 5 to 80 mV s−1, starting from the most positive to the most negative potential, with a stabilization time of 20 s at each potential limit.
The ECSA was estimated by dividing the Cdl value by the specific capacitance (Cs), with Cs assumed to be 0.035 mF cm−2.
All measurements were performed near the open-circuit potential (OCP) using CO2-saturated 0.1 mol·L−1 KHCO3 as supporting electrolyte.
In comparison, the other materials showed decreasing Cdl values: PL6C@Cu1.24 (168.50 μF·cm−2), PL6C@Cu0.48 (141.97 μF· cm−2), PL6C@Cu0.11 (137.61 μF·cm−2), and bare PL6C (122.17 μF·cm−2).
The ECSA was estimated, yielding values of 3.49, 3.93, 4.05, 8.02, and 4.81 for the bare PL6C, PL6C@ Cu0.11, PL6C@Cu0.48, PL6C@Cu1.04, and PL6C@Cu1.24 samples, respectively.

result_values.definition: ECSA estimated by dividing Cdl by the assumed specific capacitance Cs = 0.035 mF cm−2
